bull.b: The long-term Anthropic lease materially improves revenue visibility and supports TeraWulf’s transition toward contracted high-performance computing infrastructure. A large committed customer relationship can underpin future utilization, financing access, and recurring lease economics as additional capacity is delivered.

Greater committed borrowing capacity strengthens liquidity flexibility for operations, letters of credit, and growth investments. The expanded facility does not eliminate funding needs, but it provides additional financial optionality while TeraWulf builds contracted data-center capacity and manages project timing.

Doubling Muskie’s contracted power capacity expands the scale of TeraWulf’s potential AI and HPC platform and supports a multi-gigawatt development strategy. Utility-backed power access is a durable operating asset that can enable larger customer deployments if execution and financing remain on track.

bear.b: Strong gross margins have not translated into sustainable profitability because operating costs and other charges remain much larger than gross profit. Continued deep losses reduce internally generated capital, increase dependence on external financing, and make execution of the expansion plan more financially sensitive.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the current business is not self-funding while substantial investment continues. Persistent cash burn can consume liquidity, increase reliance on debt or equity financing, and constrain TeraWulf’s ability to absorb delays or cost overruns across its project pipeline.

High cash interest outflows and negative adjusted EBITDA create a demanding funding burden before additional capacity reaches revenue generation. At the same time, constrained electrical labor and complex customer-driven designs raise schedule risk, potentially delaying the cash returns needed to support expansion.
